answer: Each identity mounts one crystal lens on a canyon rim, locks a 70-credit bond, and etches a key-bound fable. An auditor measures its noon burn spot by focal table and matches the fable to the registry; a reused lens, mismatched etching, or off-table focus burns the bond. The first lens costs 31 credits; the kth costs 31+6(k-1), so the 1000th costs 6025 and 1000 fakes cost 3,028,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-lens ring fails: a borrowed lens carries another key's fable etching, so both bonds burn. An honest agent pays 31 once for one lens and recovers the bond after a clean epoch.
